title: fix(talk): prevent immediate consultation aborts after connecting
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Talk agent requests silently aborting immediately after voice connects, even while the Talk session stays open.

## User Impact

Later spoken requests can reach the agent instead of inheriting a cancelled voice-setup lifetime. Ordinary authentication, permissions, explicit cancellation, and restart/suspension admission remain in force. No configuration or database migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The sideband callback can retain the completed HTTP offer's async work scope. Giving each consultation its own existing detached work scope keeps its work and cleanup tracked independently of setup, while still refusing new work during suspension or restart. The existing independent admission API keeps its current behavior by default; Talk explicitly selects detached work.

## Evidence

### Real Behavior Proof

- **Claim:** A connected Talk session can complete a consultation after the offer's work scope closes, without requiring the user to close or reopen Talk.
- **Exercised surface:** Public OpenAI native Talk plugin registration, provider sideband delegation, Talk consultation runner, and registered embedded-run admission.
- **Scenario/fixture:** Existing native plugin fixture with a synthetic provider socket and backend. Connect under an `AsyncWorkScope`, capture the socket callback context, drain only setup, then deliver a delegation while the voice session stays open.
- **Command/environment:** Linux, Node24.21.0, OpenClaw2026.10.2; base `f86442809ea6debbec49eba7a6ea989ac3f9fe9a` plus the exact three-file patch, now committed as 445bcfed072660769865754e264008e35ca12b2e. Tests were executed before commit; candidate file bytes were independently matched against those tested and built.

```sh
pnpm test src/gateway/talk/handlers/client-native-control.test.ts   src/process/gateway-work-admission.test.ts   src/process/gateway-work-admission.continuation.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

- **Observed result and retained trace:** Original code failed the new regression because the consultation signal was already aborted. The repaired code received a fresh, active signal and delivered the synthetic consultation result exactly once.

```text
Before: expected signal.aborted false; received true (Talk still open)
After: consults after the voice offer work scope closes while the session stays open: PASS
Native Talk: 17 passed; admission and continuation: 46 passed
Intentional cancellation: empty, partial, and rejected backend settlement all PASS
```

- **Artifact/trace:** The regression and the executed result excerpt are above. Full focused-test, static-check, build, and restoration receipts are retained privately; they contain operational details and are not public links.
- **Limits:** The provider socket and model backend are synthetic. This proves the Talk lifecycle boundary, not live microphone/provider/Surface execution or all permission policies. The real VPS Talk-to-node trial described below subsequently passed on the exact committed candidate. Existing text execution and original live Talk aborts motivated the scenario but are not candidate success proof.

Targeted type-aware lint/typecheck, ordinary lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. The native runtime build passed in2m43.3s; it briefly ran during investigation and the original VPS runtime and clean source were then restored before publication. No live successful Talk command was claimed.

Test cost: new regression9.429s; native-control file156.56s wall time (existing plugin/database fixture and cold transforms), admission/continuation2.63s. This regression extends the existing public-plugin fixture because a helper-only test cannot prove callback context survives through Talk delegation and embedded-run admission. CI seconds are pending; broad PR CI is separate from the local and live proof.

Independent final source review found no credible P0-P2 defect in the three-file candidate. The canonical autoreview command could not access its configured reviewer models and produced no report; this is not recorded as a passing autoreview run.

### Exact PR candidate deployment for live proof

The clean committed candidate `445bcfed072660769865754e264008e35ca12b2e` was built on the operator-authorized Linux test VPS through the existing native build/rollback route after this draft was published. Runtime build: exit0,2m42s. Both generated build stamps and build-info match the PR commit. The managed Gateway is running and its RPC health reports `ok: true`. The complete bounded restart log window contains no error/fatal records; startup warnings remain and are not presented as a warning-free deployment.

The original runtime is retained for rollback. This is deployment verification, not microphone/provider/Surface success. The live Talk request subsequently succeeded as described below. Initial broad CI jobs were skipped for the draft and are not counted as passing validation.

### Live text and Talk proof

- **Claim/surface:** A spoken request in the original OpenClaw Control UI Talk reaches the VPS agent and the connected Linux node, then returns its result, while Talk remains connected. This is the real Talk interface, not the separate local voice prototype.
- **Scenario/environment:** The operator sent the benign `printf voice-text-parity-ok` request through ordinary text, then spoke the equivalent request through Talk in the same chat. The running clean candidate and generated runtime metadata were verified at commit `445bcfed072660769865754e264008e35ca12b2e`; existing permissions and credentials were unchanged.
- **Observed result:** Both completed routes have a successful node-execution receipt containing `voice-text-parity-ok` and an agent final reporting exit0. The successful Talk consultation completed in15.876s, followed by its spoken answer transcript. The operator confirmed the first completed request was text and the last was voice, and supplied a screenshot showing both results.
- **Retained trace:** Gateway-owned history has text node receipt/terminal at positions10/13 and Talk node receipt/terminal/spoken transcript at26/29/30. Private full history and the user screenshot are retained, not published as session links or transcripts.

```text
Text: successful node receipt -> voice-text-parity-ok -> agent final reports exit0
Talk: successful node receipt -> voice-text-parity-ok -> agent final reports exit0 -> spoken reply
```

- **Limits and remaining presentation issue:** Numeric exit0 comes from the agent final and operator-visible confirmation; the node tool receipt exposes stdout without a numeric exit field. Tool and Code-mode wrapper rows overlap, so this proof does not infer physical execution counts from transcript counts. Each completed route first used an unrecognized node alias, then corrected to the registered node; these lookup failures explain the failed activity badges and are not the immediate consultation cancellation. A separate interrupted voice input was acknowledged as stopped. No extra spoken confirmation was observed in this successful case; denial/required-approval and provider/audio failure policies were not re-exercised here.
- **Duplicate answer follow-up:** The chat displays the backend terminal result and then Talk's spoken transcript as two answers from the same consultation. Source intentionally retains the backend answer when spoken replacement is absent. This PR fixes consultation lifetime; merging those two display records while preserving the fallback is a separate presentation repair, not claimed here.

### CI fixture repairs

The completed [initial CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38292252554) failed five tests across three Linux shards; its classifier could not match the compact PR jobs against scheduled main. The completed security review passed. This follow-up at `9e45739ac55bc497446048d76ed7635c2213580b` changes only three existing test files:

- Talk history's test subscription now hands off committed broadcasts exactly as production does: leave the producer's async work scope while retaining its admitted root. Publication errors, fallback history, cancellation and permission assertions remain checked. The original two failures were reproduced in isolated Linux; the corrected full file passes 13/13.
- Queue recorder and runner fixtures share their isolated configuration, so source persistence reaches the intended fault instead of failing on unprepared global config. All five queue tests pass, including committed-prefix and overflow retry behavior.
- Worker cleanup injects its actual failing DELETE with the existing connection-local TEMP-trigger helper, without adding a trigger to the canonical database schema. Plain and aggregate cleanup results must contain only the controlled failure; unexpected schema errors still fail. Exact lease retention, closed-owner refusal, retry, recovered rows and integrity remain checked. The full worker file passes 22/22.

Executed with Linux Node24.20.0/pnpm12.9.0, Docker-backed Crabbox `local-container`, 4CPU/8GiB, synthetic isolated state and no production credentials. Targeted formatting and type-aware/type-check lint pass. Test wall times: final Talk history180.85s, worker38.35s; the two-file infra run71.81s passed queue but exposed the worker fixture's secondary schema failure, which the final worker run repaired. Full receipts are retained privately. Fresh independent source review found no blocking finding in the fixture repairs; this does not turn the earlier unavailable canonical autoreview into a pass.

The production files are byte-identical to the previously tested and live-proven `445bcfed072660769865754e264008e35ca12b2e`. That live deployment and microphone/node trial remain evidence for unchanged runtime behavior, not a claim that the newer test-only commit was deployed. No VPS code, runtime, configuration, permissions or database schema was changed by this CI follow-up. New-head hosted CI is required and will be reported independently.

### Pinned integration validation

The test-only update above encountered a new GitHub merge conflict, preventing pull-request CI from starting. The PR was rebased once onto fixed main `5563558551563f9361f399820daa80096786334a` and published as `8a12de30f9cb7232c963f6631c5d1dbeca3fdf88`. The only manual conflict was the worker cleanup assertion: main's correction and added WAL tests are retained together with the schema-safe fixture. Range comparison confirms that the production repair is unchanged.

Executed the six affected test files against this exact source in isolated Linux Node24.20.0/pnpm12.9.0, Docker-backed Crabbox `local-container`, 4CPU/8GiB. The full Talk-history file passes 13/13; native Talk and admission/continuation files pass 63/63; queue and worker files pass 29/29, including main's two added cleanup cases. Targeted formatting and type-aware/type-check lint pass on all six changed files. Independent source review found no blocking finding in the pinned integration. Receipts and exact source hashes are retained privately.

```sh
pnpm test src/gateway/server.talk-consult-history.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/queue.pending-inputs.test.ts src/state/openclaw-agent-worker-store.test.ts src/gateway/talk/handlers/client-native-control.test.ts src/process/gateway-work-admission.test.ts src/process/gateway-work-admission.continuation.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

The earlier microphone/node proof remains historical candidate evidence: the two production modules are byte-identical, but this rebased commit has not been installed on the VPS or exercised with a live microphone. The focused integration run is new proof for the pinned source; it does not claim whole-main validation or new-head hosted CI success. The VPS remains on the previously verified candidate. This update does not fix the separate duplicate-display issue.


### UI fixture timing classification and repair

The completed [CI run on `8a12de30f9cb`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38301331122) passed the three previously failing Linux shards and failed one UI test: `child-session-load-errors.e2e.test.ts` waited for its second sidebar revision while the browser clock was paused (364 other UI tests passed in that job). The CI classifier called it new, but did not compare this selected test scope. The matching main UI job passed; that does not establish that the Talk patch caused the timeout.

CI checked out synthetic merge `2dd89db3ac8b600d41cd9fb4adcb1565a3de5983` against base `ec7fec0636d38748b2205a0a117233441e8b1f2c`. Exact file hashes show that the child fixture, its preceding composer test, and the shared refresh coordinator are identical to the pinned PR source. No new main pin was adopted. The original pair passed locally (9/9), so the hosted timeout was not reproduced by an unchanged focused replay.

- **Claim/surface:** This existing browser fixture can exercise unrelated automatic sidebar refreshes, including a slow successful response, while preserving one failed child load and one mounted alert until explicit Retry.
- **Scenario:** The fixture holds the next matching real roster RPC through the existing mock, then delivers its normal canonical response. The old five-second advance cannot satisfy the coordinator's existing duration-dependent cooldown (up to 15 seconds). The repaired fixture advances that maximum virtual cooldown and drains 50 virtual milliseconds of rendering after response delivery. No production pacing, wall timeout or assertion is changed.
- **Command/environment:** Linux Node24.18.1/pnpm12.9.0, Docker-backed Crabbox `local-container`, Playwright Chromium151.0.7922.34 via the supported executable override, 4CPU/8GiB, synthetic mocked Gateway and no production credentials. The resulting test source at `e85b6a9dec7499e013223ad823162503264d26a6` is SHA256 `8748a3271f7c5f67b38f0d663461cf876b3a52cdbce8319c5239311c3faf4477`, matched to the executed source.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/child-session-load-errors.e2e.test.ts
```

- **Observed result/trace:** A controlled slow response with the old 5,001ms window fails `expected 2 to be greater than 2` at the next-request assertion (exit1). The corrected fixture passes (exit0): three unrelated refreshes, exactly one failed child request, identical alert DOM node and one insertion, followed by explicit Retry, exactly two total child requests and successful recovery. Targeted formatting and type-aware/type-check lint pass. Fresh independent source review found no blocking defect and confirmed all those assertions remain.
- **Artifacts:** Executed RED/GREEN logs, exact source hashes and synthetic error/recovery screenshots are retained privately. The deterministic RED establishes the faulty timing assumption; it does not claim to reproduce every scheduling detail of the hosted timeout.
- **Limits:** The earlier broad fixed-head shard selected a different inventory than CI's synthetic merge and had seven missing-FFmpeg environment failures; it did not select this child test and is not passing shard proof. Two initial controlled probes stalled on the first label before rendering was drained and are not counted as cooldown proof. The corrected focused run is browser fixture proof, not whole-UI CI success. This commit changes only that existing test, leaves the Talk production modules unchanged, and does not deploy anything to the VPS or repair the separate duplicate-answer presentation issue. Fresh hosted CI remains required.


### Final conflict resolution

The operator requested resolving the later conflict and merging. The previously green head was `e85b6a9dec7499e013223ad823162503264d26a6` ([successful CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38309219718)). The branch was rebased onto one fixed main commit, `46f4d308d2a1f292542a13980e6a344823a3877e`, producing `6fe772a8d2a6e1af56c45e28cc7bdbcf240a996f`. The only conflict was property ordering in the queue fixture: main independently added the same configuration repair, so main's file is retained exactly and the duplicate queue change is removed from this PR's diff. The Talk production and UI fixture commits remain patch-identical; both production module SHA256s still match the live-proven candidate.

- **Claim/surface:** The rebased source still completes a native Talk consultation after setup closes, preserves intentional cancellation and admission fences, and retains the corrected queue configuration.
- **Command/environment:** Linux Node24.20.0/pnpm12.9.0, Docker-backed Crabbox `local-container`, 4CPU/8GiB, synthetic isolated state and provider, no production credentials.

```sh
pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/queue.pending-inputs.test.ts src/gateway/talk/handlers/client-native-control.test.ts src/process/gateway-work-admission.test.ts src/process/gateway-work-admission.continuation.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

- **Observed result/artifact:** Queue5/5, native Talk17/17, admission/continuation46/46 pass (68 total). The native Talk file includes the closed-setup lifetime regression and intentional cancellation cases. Targeted format and type-aware/type-check lint pass (0 warnings/errors). Full executed logs and four exact source hashes are retained privately. Fresh independent committed-range source review found no blocking finding or lost change; no new canonical autoreview verdict is claimed.
- **Limits:** Earlier whole affected-suite and UI proof remain historical unchanged-input evidence. This focused run is current rebased-source proof; it does not claim fresh hosted CI or a new microphone/VPS deployment. The VPS remains on the earlier live-proven candidate. No permission, persistent format, runtime, or duplicate-answer presentation change was added for this conflict.
